consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed net short positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, as published by the national regulator

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

evidence.text: Irenic Capital Management -- a New York strategic activist whose signature campaign is to push a company into a sale -- disclosed a 5.41% interest in Oxford BioMedica this morning (RNS 21 Sep 2026, 10:43), 5.349720% of it through CFDs, threshold crossed 17-Sep-2026, no previous notification. It is not in any wire copy: a search for Irenic + Oxford Biomedica returns the Goldman Sachs TR-1 filed five minutes earlier (which Reuters DID carry) and nothing on Irenic at all.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one comparable ownership event on this name is the 14 Jan 2026 EQT possible-offer announcement, on which OXB rose 10.65% to 889p in early trading (cityam.com). Today's intraday tape shows the market has given the Irenic filing almost nothing: 472.5 at 09:30 UTC, 475.4 at 10:00 UTC on the day's heaviest 15-minute volume to that point, then back to 470-472 by 13:40 UTC -- about +0.6% taken and returned.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is nine search-engine-invisible hours old and it lives only in the RNS record. If it were priced, the 09:43 UTC filing would have produced a step change in the tape rather than +0.6% retraced inside an hour; a WebSearch for the fund and the company returns the Goldman TR-1 that Reuters auto-carried and zero Irenic hits; and no UK outlet has written it up. What makes tomorrow the resolution rather than some later week is that a results morning is when eight brokers publish, the domestic press writes the company up, and management is asked on the call -- the activist gets read into the story then, not on a quiet Monday. Two things sharpen it: EQT's Rule 2.8 restriction from 25 Feb 2026 ran six months and expired 25 August 2026, and the board rejected EQT's four proposals as having 'undervalued the Company' when the stock was near 889p against 472p now.
evidence.independence: Goldman Sachs Group crossed 5.083440% on 16-Sep-2026, one day before Irenic's crossing, of which 3.292213% is 'Securities Lending' and 1.789819% cash-settled swaps -- a prime-broker book building on the same dates, from a different filer: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/oxford-biomedica--oxb/holding-s-in-company/9782068 . The Rule 2.8 restriction and its expiry date are in EQT's own announcement: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/oxford-biomedica--oxb/rule-2-8-announcement/9447028

evidence.text: Tomorrow is the first time management speaks to the Novartis/BMS autoimmune CAR-T pause, which happened after the 7 August guide -- Novartis began holding eight rap-cel trials on 24 August after three IEC-HS deaths, disclosed 1 September, and OXB fell 14.7% that day and a further 5.1% the next with no RNS of its own. The sell-side quantification is small and survivable: c.10-16m of annual clinical revenue at risk (7-10m Novartis, 2-6m BMS), autoimmune 13% of 48 programmes, and pre-booked manufacturing slots protecting FY2026 with disruption pushed to new bookings in H2 2027. Reiterating 180-200m six weeks after cutting to it is the base case and is not what the 1-2 September tape priced.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line that has moved this stock all year and it has moved it down: -14.6% on 7 Aug 2026 when FY26 went from 220-240m to 180-200m (591 to 505 on 6.6m shares), and -5.12% on the 26 Mar 2026 prelims. OXB has not had a positive scheduled-release reaction in the observed record, which is why this is sized as a relief rather than a re-rating.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock is 472p against 524p on 28 August, so roughly half the Novartis/BMS drawdown is still in the price six weeks on, and the company has said nothing -- its RNS record between 14 August and today contains one Total Voting Rights notice and four Holding(s) in Company, no trading statement. If the market believed FY26 was protected by pre-booked slots it would have closed the 1-2 September gap. Against it: the cell-and-gene CDMO sector is in genuine retrenchment (Rentschler withdrawing, Catalent closing Belgium, Charles River divesting its CDMO to GI Partners, Lonza reporting softer cell-and-gene), which is a broader public series and is the reason the low end of my band is -3.5 rather than -1.
evidence.independence: Net of the rest of the company: for the 180-200m guide to hold, H2 must deliver 100-120m against H1's 80m, i.e. +25% to +50% half-on-half, with the Durham NC site ramping on its revised schedule. Corroborated from the issuer's own document rather than a broker -- 193m revenue backlog and 97m of contracted client orders at 30 June, 17 new clients in H1 (more than 30% above the whole of FY25): https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/oxford-biomedica--oxb/half-year-trading-update-and-notice-of-results/9709646

evidence.text: The 6.86% aggregate net short is entirely sub-threshold: Investegate's mirror of the FCA per-holder public file reads 'Active Short Positions: None currently disclosed' for OXB, and no individual holder has ever disclosed more than 1.05% on this name in eleven years. So the crowd is many books each under 0.5% -- a quant and dealer profile rather than one fundamental bear -- and it is invisible on the screens a UK private investor or adviser actually looks at.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed squeeze on this name; the register has never carried a crowded position here before. Sized off the US record instead, where two names with 18% and 23% of float short both squeezed more than 20%, and discounted heavily for the dependence flagged below.
evidence.why_not_priced: Two public files disagree about this name and only one of them is read per-company. The FCA aggregate says 6.86% and building; the per-holder file that Investegate, and every retail short screen downstream of it, mirrors says zero. A market that had reconciled them would not leave a 2.4x build since the profit warning unremarked in every piece of coverage I could find. I have deliberately NOT sized this as though it were an independent bear signal -- see independence.
evidence.independence: NOT independent of finding 1 and sized down for it. The aggregate's position date (16/09/2026) is the same day Goldman crossed 5% holding 3.29% via securities lending, and one day before Irenic's CFD crossing -- so a material part of this 'short' is plausibly a dealer delta-hedge of a long CFD rather than a bearish bet, which would make it fuel in the same direction as finding 1 rather than a second reason. evidence.text: On 9 September 2026 M+C Saatchi announced that the Parc-backed management buyout of its Australia and New Zealand advertising agency had failed due diligence and that the business will instead CEASE OPERATIONS before the end of 2026, with the entire ANZ leadership team and all staff departing and Woolworths finishing in November. There is no RNS on the subject -- not for the 22 July MBO agreement and not for the 9 September collapse and closure -- and no UK financial outlet has covered it. The 22 September interim statement is the first regulated document in which the UK market can see it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Australia has been the line that moves this stock. The 18 Sep 2025 interims, which carried the Australian restructure and the closure of the Bohemia media unit, produced -12.24% -- by far the largest of the 13 observed reactions (median |move| 1.98%). The 24 Nov 2025 trading update, which downgraded the FY25 decline to 7%, produced -5.16%. But the 20 Apr 2026 FY results, which disclosed FY25 separately-disclosed items of GBP9.1m 'largely restructuring costs in Australia' alongside the language 'simplify the businesses ... unlock the intrinsic value', produced +3.91%. So this line has moved the stock hard in both directions, and the sign has tracked whether Australia was presented as a continuing problem or as a problem being removed. This time it is being removed entirely.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Investegate RNS record for M&C Saatchi from 1 July 2026 to 21 September 2026 contains nothing but Transaction in Own Shares, three Holding(s) in Company and the Notice of Half Year Results -- no announcement of the MBO, none of its collapse, none of the closure. Every outlet carrying it is Australian trade press (Campaign Brief, Campaign Brief NZ, Campaign Brief Asia, Mumbrella, Mediaweek, B&T, Mi3). Sharecast covered this issuer's March 2026 CEO change, so it follows the name, and it did not carry this. If the market had priced the closure of an entire country's advertising operations announced with no consideration and all staff departing, the stock would not be sitting at 147p on 21 September, within 2% of its 52-week high of 150p and up 29% from its April low of 113.5p; nor would a break-up activist have crossed 9% on 18 September. What the tape shows instead is a 149p-to-142p drift from 8 to 11 September fully given back by 18 September on ordinary volume -- consistent with a handful of holders reading the Australian trade press, not with the information being in the price. Size: APAC was 18% of FY25 like-for-like group net revenue (GBP204.7m) and fell 22.3%, 'predominantly Australia'; Australia alone fell 31.9% and accounts for the whole gap between the -3.1% group decline ex-Australia and the -7.3% including it. Removing it structurally lifts continuing-group organic growth by roughly 3-4pp and lifts margin; against that sit closure costs on top of FY25's GBP9.1m of separately-disclosed items (largely Australian restructuring), cash out rather than in, and an FY27 consensus of GBP221.8m / +3.6% organic that has to come down on the revenue line. That two-sidedness is why the band spans -4.5 to +5.5 and the point estimate is only +1.2. Net of the rest of the company: this rests on one region, and it requires H1 net revenue and margin to be at least in line, which the 11 June AGM update (Jan-Apr, LFL net revenue in line and supportive of the full year outlook) and an easy cost comparative support -- H1 2025 LFL operating margin was 9.9% after first-half-weighted investment in senior talent that has since annualised, and group central costs fell from GBP12.4m to GBP6.1m.
evidence.independence: Independently reported the same day by Mumbrella ('M&C Saatchi is preparing to exit Australia, ending a 30-year run'; 'the Australian business will be folded by November'; 'Woolworths will be the last remaining client ... with its contract ending in November') at https://mumbrella.com.au/mc-saatchi-australia-set-to-close-936541 , and by Campaign Brief Asia at https://campaignbriefasia.com/2026/09/09/mc-saatchi-australia-new-zealand-advertising-agency-management-buyout-no-longer-proceeding/ . The underlying Australian deterioration is corroborated in the issuer's own primary document: the FY25 preliminary results state 'APAC: Net revenue fell 22.3% as the macroeconomic environment in the core Australia market remained very weak' and 'The Group closed its Australian media buying business in September 2025' -- https://www.mcsaatchiplc.com/~/media/Files/M/mc-saatchi/documents/result-centre/2025/fy-2025-results-announcement.pdf

evidence.text: A TR-1 published at 17:25 on 21 September 2026 -- after the London close that sets this window's entry price, and 13.5 hours before the results RNS -- discloses that Harwood Capital / Rockwood Strategic / Oryx (all controlled by Christopher Mills) crossed 9% on 18 September, taking the holding to 9.0865% / 10,907,000 shares from 9,700,000 shares at the 11 June notification. Harwood has been publicly urging a BREAK-UP of M&C Saatchi since March 2026 and has stepped its stake up four times this year: 6.001% -> 7.118% (8 May) -> 8.023% (11 June) -> 9.0865% (18 September).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior instance of a 9%-threshold TR-1 from this holder landing on the eve of a results print for this issuer, so there is no direct history. What there is: the three previous Harwood step-ups (12 May, 15 June, 5 August window) landed on ordinary days and moved nothing visible, which is the point -- none of them coincided with a catalyst. The comparable line is governance news, and the 9 March 2026 announcement of the CEO's departure with Vin Murria returning as deputy chair was the trigger for a re-rating from 113.5p in April to 150p in September.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was published at 17:25, i.e. after the 16:30 close, so it is not in the entry price by construction -- the baseline's spot was struck at 13:39 UTC. It is also arithmetically a real purchase and not a buyback artefact: the 2,222,500 shares cancelled under the programme only take 9,700,000 shares from 8.023% to 8.081% of the reduced 120,034,965 voting rights, so Harwood genuinely bought 1,207,000 shares between 11 June and 18 September. Against a median 20-day turnover of USD264,728 (about GBP198k, roughly 135,000 shares a day at 146.7p) that is about nine days of the entire market's volume in this stock, and 274,644 shares traded on 21 September against a 20-day median near 135,000. On a GBP174m AIM name with five analysts, a named activist who has publicly demanded a break-up crossing 9% the night before the interims is exactly the fact nobody is positioned for. If it were priced, the register would not be the only place it exists: there is no broker note, no UK article and no wire copy on it, and the FCA short register is a flat 0.20% residual showing no one on the other side.
evidence.independence: Harwood's break-up campaign is independently sourced to The Times via QuotedData, 16 March 2026: 'Harwood Capital is also urging the break-up of advertising group M&C Saatchi', with the stake then at 6% -- https://quoteddata.com/2026/03/morning-briefing-liontrust-buys-martin-gilberts-river-global-harwood-pushes-for-mc-saatchi-break-up/ . The board is configured for the same outcome and this is corroborated by a separate document: the FY25 preliminary results say the Group's 'key focus ... is to unlock the intrinsic value of the Company that is not currently recognised' and that 'the Board remains focused on accelerating initiatives to maximise shareholder value', with Vin Murria (who led the 2022 AdvancedAdvT bid for the company) returning as deputy chair and ex-Lazard banker Nick Shott as NED, and no permanent CEO since Zaid Al-Qassab left on 31 March 2026 -- https://www.sharecast.com/news/aim-bulletin/mc-saatchi-ceo-stepping-down-vin-murria-joins-board--21972116.html

evidence.text: The share buyback programme launched on 9 March 2026 was terminated on 15 September 2026 -- seven days before the interims -- having used only GBP2,877,594 of a GBP4.5m authority (2,222,500 shares at an average 131.1p). It ran out of time, not money. With consensus DPS at nil for both FY26 and FY27 and the Board on record at the FY25 results that it 'believes that greater value can be created for shareholders by increasing the share buyback programme rather than through the payment of a dividend', the interim statement is the natural venue for a replacement programme -- and if none comes, the stock's only mechanical bid has just been withdrawn into a print carrying a closure charge.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 20 Apr 2026 FY results, which announced the reallocation of the final dividend into an enlarged buyback, produced +3.91% -- the best results-day reaction in the 13-event observed record. The 9 March 2026 launch of the programme itself coincided with the start of the re-rating from the April low of 113.5p. Capital return is the one line this stock has consistently paid up for.
evidence.why_not_priced: The RNS itself is public, so the fact is not hidden -- what is unpriced is the conjunction, which needs a domestic reader to assemble: an authority left 36% unused, terminated on a fixed date one week before results, on a company whose Board has stated in a primary document that it intends to substitute buybacks for dividends, at a point where a fresh authority would normally be announced with the interims. The programme was buying roughly GBP22k a day against GBP198k of market turnover, about a tenth of the volume in the stock, so its removal is mechanically visible in a name this thin. If the market were positioned for a relaunch there would be commentary on it; there is none from any of the five covering brokers that is publicly visible. This is the smallest and the softest of the three findings -- it rests on an inference about what the Board will do, not on a fact about what it has done -- and it is sized accordingly, with a band that crosses zero.
evidence.independence: The Board's stated intention is in a different document -- the FY25 preliminary results: 'the Board intends to reallocate the amount that would otherwise have been proposed as a final dividend for the year ended 31 December 2025' to the buyback, with statutory dividends already at nil (2024: 1.95p) -- https://www.mcsaatchiplc.com/~/media/Files/M/mc-saatchi/documents/result-centre/2025/fy-2025-results-announcement.pdf

Yahoo returns 0 expiries and 0 contracts for .L, .DE and .PA symbols against 21 and 196 for AAPL on the same crumb; Eurex's daily reference file carries trading parameters but no settlement prices, no open interest and no underlying ISIN map, and its statistics page is JavaScript with no JSON endpoint. This holds for all ten markets; nothing measured in 2026-09 on …

consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed net short positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, as published by the national regulator

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fonix's Final Results are always pre-announced by a July trading update, and both observed Final Results in the baseline's observed_rns history moved slightly DOWN: -0.63% on 2024-09-24 and -1.83% on 2025-09-23. evidence.why_not_priced: The FACT is fully priced — that is the finding. What is not priced is the event's own size: with two analysts and no option chain there is no implied move, and any ranker using the baseline's 5.27% proxy will size this print as if it could travel as far as a January trading update. If the market genuinely expected a 5% move into an audit confirmation you would see it in the tape — you would not see a stock sitting in a 167.5-177.0p band for a month on 60-120k shares a day. Instead the pre-print session printed 203,444 shares, still only ~GBP 350k of turnover, which is a thin de-risking, not an event being positioned for.
evidence.independence: Kalkine, 12 August 2026, independently records the price reaction to the same update: the shares fell despite the beat and were 'close to the lower end of a 52-week range spanning roughly 143p to 244p' — https://kalkine.co.uk/news/technology/fonix-dips-as-investors-digest-a-full-year-trading-update-that-beat-expectations. evidence.text: The one number that sets both the dividend and the P/E — adjusted EPS — is the number the market has NOT seen, and it is where the growth is leaking away: H1 FY26 adjusted EPS was exactly FLAT at 6.2p while gross profit rose 7.1% and adjusted EBITDA rose 6.4%, because adjusted PBT grew only 2.6% on rising amortisation of capitalised software (carrying value GBP 2.2m vs GBP 1.8m) and 'a modest rise in the effective corporation tax rate'. The 23 July update disclosed gross profit, adjusted EBITDA and TPV and gave no EPS figure at all.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time Fonix put a flat adjusted EPS in front of the market was the 17 March 2026 interims (6.2p vs 6.2p) and the stock moved +1.94% — i.e. it was looked through, because the interims also carried a +6.9% interim dividend and an upgraded international narrative. The comparable disappointment is 18 March 2025, -5.21%, the one interim where the delivery did not match the framing. So this line has been both looked through and punished within twelve months; the band is deliberately wide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Adjusted EPS is the denominator of the dividend policy ('at least 75% of adjusted earnings per share') and of the 14.1x forward P/E the screens carry, and it is the only headline Fonix has never pre-announced. FY25 adjusted EPS was 11.3p (FY24 10.8p, +4.6%) and the house broker's FY26 number is 11.5p — +1.8% against adjusted EBITDA up 11.0%. If that gap were in the price you would not see a stock screened on a forward P/E and a 5.63% forecast yield with a 293p consensus target against a 171p close; you would see the target cut. With one house broker publishing (the company's own AIM Rule 26 page lists Cavendish as the only analyst), there is no second estimate to arbitrage the gap.
evidence.independence: The FY25 Annual Report gives the same mechanism a year earlier and the arithmetic to check it against: adjusted EPS 11.3p, adjusted ROCE, underlying cash down 12.4% to GBP 9,877k from GBP 11,324k, and a stated payout of '78% of adjusted EPS as an ordinary dividend' plus a 3p special so that 'total dividends for the year amount to more than 100% of adjusted EPS' — https://www.fonix.com/?jet_download=fe2e3c21121d1ba8d566afde207739f4259b899e (17 Oct 2025). evidence.text: Fonix's ability to buy back stock is structurally capped by Rule 9 of the Takeover Code and almost nobody outside the RNS knows it: the concert party holds 33.05% of the share capital, so the company 'has historically been restricted in its ability to conduct share buyback programmes', and the GBP 2.0m 'buyback' every aggregator reported as completed was in fact a SINGLE purchase of exactly 1,250,000 shares (1.25% of capital) at a fixed 159p, only possible because Richard Thompson, through Starnevesse Limited, signed an irrevocable undertaking to sell alongside so the concert party's interest did not increase — his holding fell 7.362603% to 6.149129% in the matching TR-1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital return is the line that moves this stock most. The single largest observed reaction in the baseline's history is 2025-01-23, +5.83%, headlined 'Trading Update and Special Dividend Declaration' — the trading update alone a year later (2026-01-22, no special) moved +5.33%, and 2024-01-24 'Trading Update' moved +9.30%, so the specials are not the whole of it, but this is demonstrably a shareholder-return-owned register. FY26 broke the pattern: no special dividend was declared in January 2026 for the first time, and a GBP 2.0m structured buyback in May replaced it — on 22 May 2026 the shares closed at 159p, the buyback price, and did not re-rate.
evidence.why_not_priced: The structure is only in the RNS PDF. TipRanks describes it as 'completed a GBP 2.0 million share buyback, reflecting strong cash generation and the board's confidence' (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/fonix-lifts-profits-and-steps-up-european-push-as-mobile-payments-pipeline-grows) and Kalkine as a 'GBP 2.0 million programme' — neither mentions Rule 9, the 33.05% concert party or the matching irrevocable, and the issuer's own 23 July summary of it says only 'the Group also completed a GBP 2.0m on-market share buyback, underlining the Board's confidence'. So the read available to anyone who did not open the May RNS is 'this company now runs buybacks', when the true read is 'this company can only run a buyback when a named 6.1% holder agrees to sell into it'. If the market knew, the finals' capital-return line would not carry an open-ended-buyback option in the price at all. The direction is modestly negative because it removes an upside scenario rather than creating a downside one: the promised increase in the FINAL DIVIDEND is the one return that needs nobody's permission, and it is contractually ~75-78% of an adjusted EPS that grew ~2% in H1.
evidence.independence: The matching TR-1, a different document filed the same day by a different party: Starnevesse Limited, threshold crossed 22-May-2026, resulting 6.149129% / 6,003,005 shares against a previous notification of 7.362603% — https://www.fonix.com/?jet_download=3d9ff2739423f0be1229997702baa61f25dca27a. Broadcast reports the Love Island 2026 summer series launched to 620,000 viewers on ITV2, its lowest ever for a regular summer series and roughly half the prior year (https://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/digital-and-demographic-focus/love-island-2026-launches-modestly/5217604.article), and the bulk of that series sits in Fonix's Q1 FY27, which the finals' current-trading line covers. Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and this one is not established.

Ofcom took over premium-rate services regulation from the Phone-paid Services Authority on 1 February 2025 and replaced Code 15 with the PRS Order (https://www.ofcom.org.uk/phones-and-broadband/mobile-phones/ofcom-takes-on-responsibility-for-regulating-premium-rate-services) — that is 19 months old, Fonix has traded through it, and I found nothing dated in 2026 that changes the economics before this print.

The FCA aggregated register is public only at 0.5% per holder, so anything smaller is structurally unobtainable; I did not spend a call on the per-holder history file because a name absent from the current aggregate has by construction no open position at or above the threshold to find.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: absent from a register that downloaded successfully, so no disclosed net short position at or above the 0.5% public threshold. A real zero -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0, and the join is on the issuer NAME, so a name spelled differently in the register reads as a zero it should not.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: absent from a register that downloaded successfully, so no disclosed net short position at or above the 0.5% public threshold. A real zero -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0, and the join is on the issuer NAME, so a name spelled differently in the register reads as a zero it should not.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

first_hunter_context.bar: Two-part and sourced. (a) The reported half is the company's own pre-announcement: 'Revenues for the period are expected to be GBP30.8m (H1 2025: GBP32.1m)... Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be GBP5.0m-GBP5.4m (H1 2025 GBP1.6m)... unaudited net cash as at 30 June 2026 of GBP23.1m' - https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/kooth--koo/half-year-trading-update/9692237 (2026-07-29). (b) The FY bar is Kooth's own compiled consensus (Stifel, Canaccord, Singer, Cavendish), consolidated 10 April 2026: FY2026 revenue GBP63.1m, adj EBITDA GBP10.4m, diluted EPS 6.8p; FY2027 revenue GBP60.8m, adj EBITDA GBP11.4m - https://investors.kooth.com/investors/analyst-consensus.asp. Caveat carried into every size: (b) is 5.5 months stale and Kooth has not republished it since the July update.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: No disclosed net short position, and the local pass strengthened that from a truncated zero into something close to a real one. The baseline records anchor_covered:false / register_read_no_position against the FCA aggregated file of 2026-09-19 (419 issuers, Kooth absent). I additionally downloaded the FCA PER-HOLDER history, https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/data/short-positions-daily-update.xlsx, 108,851 rows spanning position dates 2012-10-31 to 2026-07-09, and Kooth appears ZERO times - by name and by ISIN GB00BMCZLK30 (the only 'ooth' matches in the file are Boothbay Fund Management rows against ASOS, Boohoo and Naked Wines). So no holder has ever crossed the 0.5% public threshold in this name in fourteen years. Consequence, stated plainly: there is no squeeze fuel, no informed short flow to agree with or beat, and NO positioning anchor at all - priced_lean_pct (-1.221) is 100% the runup term (lean_components short_squeeze 0.0, short_building 0.0, runup -1.221), which is also this stage's free control. Sub-0.5% shorting remains invisible and this is not evidence that nobody is short.
first_hunter_context.session_check: bmo. Settled from the issuer's own RNS, not the vendor: 'Kooth Plc (AIM: KOO)... will announce its half year results for the six months ended 30 June 2026 on 23 September 2026. Kate Newhouse, CEO, and Sanjay Jawa, CFO, will host an in-person analyst briefing at 9:00am BST on the morning of results' - RNS 'Notice of Half Year Results', timestamped 2026-09-08 07:01:24 on Investegate, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/kooth--koo/notice-of-half-year-results/9759930. A 09:00 BST analyst briefing on the morning of results puts the release before the 08:00 open. Corroborated by the company's financial calendar (https://investors.kooth.com/financials/financial-calendar.asp, '23 September - Half Year Results'). Window is close(2026-09-22) -> close(2026-09-23).

evidence.text: The +24.41% 20-day run-up is two sessions and no company news: 146.0p (26 Aug) -> 162.5p (27 Aug, 1,059,995 shares) -> 195.0p (28 Aug, 678,941 shares) against a ~20k/day norm, and the Investegate day archive shows NO Kooth RNS on either 27 or 28 August 2026. The cause was a Canaccord Genuity flash note on the $18bn Meta settlement (announced 26 Aug). The print is the first management communication since, and management cannot contract-confirm it: California's share is $1.5-2.1bn spread over ten years, earmarked only for 'prevention or remediation of mental health or other harms to young Californians', still awaiting a judge's approval, with not a dollar allocated to any vendor.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Kooth reprices violently on US-state funding news and the moves do not persist: -16% in a day on the Pennsylvania termination notice (18 Oct 2024) and +16.79% on the 2025 Full Year Results (15 Apr 2026), against a median absolute results-day move of 2.61% over the twelve observed RNS prints in the baseline. The nearest analogue for an un-validated gap is the present one: the stock has already surrendered 5.9% of the 195p peak and the 5-day run-up is -0.81%, so the fade has begun without the company having said anything.
evidence.why_not_priced: The move itself is obviously priced - that is the point. What is not priced is the QUALITY of it, which the run-up number cannot see. If an institution had taken the other side of 1.74m shares (4.8% of the 36,694,683 in issue) a TR-1 would have followed within the DTR5 window; none has, to 22 September. The only Holding(s) in Company RNS since (16 Sept, 13:23) is a technical transfer of the existing River UK Micro Cap holding to Liontrust at 6.0659% on an FCA change-of-control approval, not a purchase. So the marginal buyer of the gap is undisclosed and sub-3% - retail and momentum, not a re-rating by a holder who will sit through a disappointing statement. If the market had priced a durable re-rating the stock would have held 195p rather than drifting to 183.5p on falling volume, and at least one 3% notification would exist.
evidence.independence: The cause is corroborated by a second, independent domestic outlet on a different date: Share Talk's weekly small-cap movers, 31 Aug 2026 - 'Kooth (AIM: KOO) rebounded 32.2% to 195p after Canaccord Genuity highlighted potential opportunities arising from the $18 billion Meta settlement' - https://www.share-talk.com/share-talk-weekly-small-cap-movers-shakers-monday-31st-august-2026/. The settlement's terms are independently sourced to the California Attorney General's own release, https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-secures-transformative-17-billion-settlement-meta (2026-08-26).

evidence.text: The FY2026 revenue bar requires an H2 that reverses the trend of the last five halves. Kooth's own compiled consensus (10 Apr 2026) is FY26 revenue GBP63.1m; H1 2026 came in at GBP30.8m, so H2 must deliver GBP32.3m against an H2 2025 of GBP31.2m (FY25 GBP63.3m less H1 25 GBP32.088m) - +3.5% year on year - while California product development revenue continues 'planned tapering' and sterling is running ~1% stronger against the dollar in H2 2026 (~1.342) than in H2 2025 (~1.33). H1 2026 revenue itself FELL 4.0% year on year. The 29 July trading update reaffirmed only the HALF ('Performance for the half year ended 30 June 2026 is in line with expectations') and made no FY26 statement at all; 23 September is the first FY26 outlook statement since 8 April.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is precisely the line that sold the 2025 print. At the 23 Sept 2025 H1 results - also preceded by a July trading update - Kooth's outlook section quantified an FX haircut for the first time ('the expected impact would be to reduce full year consensus median revenue of GBP66.8m by c.2-3% and consensus median adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.2m by c.6-8%') and the stock fell 5.00% on the day, the baseline's second-largest negative reaction. The 29 July 2026 half-year trading update, which likewise declined to address the full year, fell 3.50%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Net of the rest of the company, this is a genuine two-sided call and that is why I size it small: H2 2026 gets the first full half of the State of Michigan contract ($2.6m annualised, signed only in January 2026 after the delays Kooth blamed for FY25), the DWP-funded employment-and-mental-health programmes launching across the West Midlands, South Yorkshire and Cambridgeshire, 14 new UK contracts, and the UK Soluna launch into the autumn school term. Those could carry GBP32.3m. What is unpriced is that with FOUR analysts covering a name doing $228k/day, nobody has published a refreshed FY26 model since April - the consensus page the market is anchored to is 5.5 months old and predates both the July update and the Meta-note re-rating. If the market had worked the arithmetic the stock would not be 63% below its own consensus 303-330p target with zero published preview.
evidence.independence: The H1 2025 comparative that fixes H2 2025 at GBP31.2m is from a different document - the audited-basis H1 2025 results PDF, https://investors.kooth.com/docs/koothplclibraries/archive/results/half-year-results-2025.pdf (total revenue 32,088). Shares the 29 July 2026 trading update RNS with nothing else in this list, since I dropped the reported-quarter finding that also rested on it.

evidence.text: Adjusted EBITDA is where Kooth has systematically sandbagged, and the FY26 bar looks low. At the 23 Sept 2025 H1 results Kooth guided FY25 consensus adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.2m down by 'c.6-8%' for FX - an implied GBP9.4-9.6m - and then delivered GBP11.3m, described in its own FY25 RNS as 'ahead of expectations': an ~18% beat against its own guided number. FY26 consensus adjusted EBITDA is GBP10.4m; H1 2026 alone is GBP5.0-5.4m against H1 2025's GBP1.6m, so H2 has only to match H1 to clear it, and the H1 2025 margin drag (gross margin -19.6ppt on front-loaded California user marketing, 'intentionally weighted towards H1 2025') is not repeating. Net cash also ROSE in the half, GBP21.6m at Dec 2025 to GBP23.1m at Jun 2026, so the -GBP6.58m cash generation that accompanied the 2025 print is absent.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: When Kooth has confirmed or beaten on adjusted EBITDA the market has paid: +11.74% on the 28 Jan 2026 Trading Update and +4.67% on the 8 Apr 2026 Full Year Results, the two most recent scheduled releases in the baseline where the EBITDA line was the good news. The offsetting precedent is that an EBITDA beat has never been enough on its own when the outlook section carried a haircut (23 Sept 2025, -5.00%), which is why this is sized below the two negatives combined rather than above them.
evidence.why_not_priced: The valuation says nobody has done this sum. At 183.5p on 36,694,683 shares the market capitalisation is ~GBP67m and, less GBP23.1m of net cash, the enterprise value is ~GBP44m - 4.2x the FY26 consensus adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.4m, for a business whose H1 adjusted EBITDA tripled. If the market had priced an EBITDA beat the stock would be trading on the run-up it got from a Meta read-through rather than despite a 4.2x EV/EBITDA, and at least one of the four brokers would have published a raised number since 10 April; none has. The honest counterweight, and the reason this is +1.3 and not +3: FY26 consensus diluted EPS of 6.8p puts the same stock on 27x earnings, so the gap between adjusted EBITDA and statutory profit is large (capitalised development amortisation), and the results statement is exactly where that gap becomes visible line by line.
evidence.independence: The FY25 outcome is from a separate RNS on a separate date: '2025 revenue was GBP63.3m (2024: GBP66.7m)... Adjusted EBITDA was ahead of expectations at GBP11.3m in 2025 (2024: GBP15.8m)' - https://investors.kooth.com/rns-alerts/archive/2026/080426.asp (2026-04-08). The FY26 consensus level is from the company's analyst-consensus page, which this finding shares with the revenue finding above; the two use the same page for OPPOSITE lines (revenue vs EBITDA) and are otherwise independent.

evidence.text: The California cliff is the dominant value driver and it resolves far outside this window. California's CYBHI Behavioral Health Virtual Services Platform funding - Soluna plus Brightline's BrightLife Kids, a $680m state commitment of which Kooth's share has been reported at $271m over four years - runs to 30 June 2027, and Kooth has 'now entered the fourth year of the contract'. FY2027 consensus revenue of GBP60.8m (only -3.6% on FY26) implicitly assumes continuity or replacement. Any re-procurement decision, and any actual allocation of California's $1.5-2.1bn Meta settlement share to a youth mental-health platform, lands in 2027 and later - not on 23 September. Management may reference it; it cannot be resolved in one session.

The Meta settlement itself was still awaiting judicial approval when it was announced on 26 August 2026, and California's payment is structured over ten years. Court approval and any state-level appropriation of those funds are the events that would validate the 27-28 August re-rating, and both sit well past 23 September 2026.

Sharecast, Proactive Investors and the Investors' Chronicle - not attempted beyond one check; documented as 403 to both curl and WebFetch in this stage's own reachability table and in researcher_europe/LESSONS.md.
Citywire - documented as returning almost nothing; not attempted.

https://investors.kooth.com/rns-alerts/archive/2026/ returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch; routed around via the Investegate day archive, which worked (validated against 2026-07-29, where it correctly returned the known Half Year Trading Update).

A takeover / Rule 2.4 / Form 8.3 explanation for the 27-28 August spike: searched and found nothing. No Takeover Code disclosure of any kind appears for KOO in the Investegate day archive between 24 August and 22 September 2026.

A TR-1 / Holding(s) in Company notification following the 1.74m shares traded on 27-28 August: none exists to 22 September. The only such RNS in the period (16 Sept) is the technical River UK Micro Cap -> Liontrust transfer at 6.0659%.
Director/PDMR Shareholding and Transaction in Own Shares: none between 24 August and 22 September 2026 - no buyback is running despite GBP23.1m of net cash against a ~GBP67m market capitalisation.

A UK contract shock. Checked the domestic procurement record (HTN Health Tech News, Find a Tender): North Central London ICB GBP405k awarded to Kooth Digital Health to 31 March 2028, NHS Somerset GBP49,157 (8 June 2026), Surrey and Borders extension to 31 March 2027. The UK book is many small tickets and is renewing, not eroding. A competitor win exists but is trivial (Wysa, GBP30k, Black Country Healthcare, 5 June 2026). Nothing sizeable enough to file.

NHS England's up-to-GBP110m children's digital health procurement (HTN, 11 June 2026) is preventative child health - the digital Red Book, screening - not mental health, contracts estimated July 2027 to June 2030. Not a Kooth read-through and outside the window twice over.

A published sell-side preview of the 23 September print: none found from Stifel, Canaccord, Singer or Cavendish. The most recent public targets are Stifel 360p (21 Apr 2026) and Canaccord 330p (8 Apr 2026), both pre-dating the July update and the August re-rating.

An FX-driven downgrade repeat: checked and largely ruled OUT rather than found. GBP/USD averaged ~1.347 in H1 2026 and ~1.342 in H2 to date against ~1.345 when consensus was struck on 10 April, so the 2025 mechanism (1.26 -> 1.35) is not present. This is why the revenue finding is sized -1.2 and not larger.

baseline.window: close of the session before 2026-09-23 -> 2026-09-23 close

options.reason: No European single-stock option chain is retrievable from a free source. Yahoo returns 0 expiries and 0 contracts for .L, .DE and .PA symbols against 21 and 196 for AAPL on the same crumb; Eurex's daily reference file carries trading parameters but no settlement prices, no open interest and no underlying ISIN map, and its statistics page is JavaScript with no JSON endpoint. first_hunter_context.bar: FY2026 adjusted basic EPS of 202.8p and FY2027 of 231.4p, both stated by the company as 'current consensus market expectations' in footnotes to its own 23 July 2026 RNS; H1 2026 adjusted EPS pre-announced at 38p-42p in the same RNS. https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/judges-scientific--jdg/half-year-trading-update-and-notice-of-results/9682935 (2026-07-23)
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Disclosed net short 1.67% of shares outstanding at position date 17/08/2026, down from 2.19% (FCA aggregated register as read by the sealed baseline, as_of 2026-09-19, https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv). Covering, not building -- but stale: the register has not moved for five weeks while the stock fell a further 3.8%. Holder detail from the FCA per-holder file (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/data/short-positions-daily-update.xlsx, downloaded 2026-09-22) and Investegate's mirror (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/JDG/short-positions) shows ONE dominant seller, GLG Partners LP, which peaked at 1.82% on 2026-02-11 and then filed 1.78% (24-Mar), 1.68% (16-Apr), 1.58% (27-Apr), 1.47% (08-May), 1.36% (19-May) -- a seven-month monotonic wind-down into a 41% price fall, i.e. profit-taking, not a forced buy-in. JPMorgan Asset Management (UK) Ltd ran 1.20% (01-Apr) down to 1.08% (22-Apr). Both mirrors end 2026-05-19, five weeks behind the aggregate. Scale: 1.67% of the 6,660,695 shares in issue (Total Voting Rights RNS, 1 June 2026) is 111,234 shares against a 20-day median volume of 8,030, i.e. 13.9 sessions to cover.
first_hunter_context.session_check: bmo, confirmed from two issuer documents rather than the vendor flag. (1) The company's own Notice of Results inside the 23 July 2026 RNS: 'The Company intends to announce its interim results for the six months to 30 June 2026 on Wednesday 23 September 2026' -- https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/judges-scientific--jdg/half-year-trading-update-and-notice-of-results/9682935. (2) The issuer's own financial calendar, '23 September 2026 - Announcement of results - 2026 interims' -- https://www.judges.uk.com/financial-performance/financial-calendar.html. Every JDG results RNS in the Investegate record is timestamped 07:00 AM (Interim Results 18 Sep 2025 07:00, Unaudited Preliminary Results 31 Mar 2026 07:00, Half Year Trading Update 23 Jul 2026 07:00), and the results webinar is separately scheduled for 17:00 UK the same day, i.e. after the RNS. So the release is pre-open and the scored window close(2026-09-22)->close(2026-09-23) is the right one.

evidence.text: The company's own 23 July RNS pre-announces H1 adjusted EPS of 38p-42p and, in a footnote, puts FY2026 consensus at 202.8p -- so the 'in line' the market is holding requires roughly 162p of H2 adjusted EPS, about four times H1 and an ~80/20 split, against 141.4p/133.9p (51/49) in 2025; the same RNS reports the order book at 17.3 weeks, which reads as improvement only against the FY25 year-end 15.7 but is flat against the like-for-like H1 2025 comparator of 17.4 weeks printed in the same sentence, and on a sales base 21% lower is roughly 21% smaller in absolute terms, with order intake down 11%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Judges has downgraded or disappointed at three of its last five scheduled statements and the stock moved -11.61% (Trading Update 2024-11-18), -15.19% (Half Year Trading Update 2025-07-24) and about -11% (Full Year Trading Statement 2026-01-22, Proactive) on those days -- so when this line surprises on this name it surprises double-digit and the UK tail is not truncated. But the two September interims in the observed RNS history moved only -4.27% (2024-09-19) and +1.91% (2025-09-18), because the July trading update had already carried the half-year news both times; and the 2026-07-23 update itself, which contained the 38-42p, the -21% revenue and the Geotek slip to 2028, moved the stock only -1.62% (4625.0 -> 4550.0, Yahoo daily closes) and it closed higher the next day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 202.8p footnote and the 38-42p are both public, but no source I could reach does the division. Every piece of secondary coverage I found reported the flattering order-book comparator (Sharecast/Halifax and the Stockopedia brief both frame it as '17.3 weeks compared with 15.7 weeks at the end of 2025') and none states the implied H2 EPS or the 80/20 split. This is a 4-analyst, GBP 250m AIM name trading about USD 446k a day, so the marginal price-setter is a retail or adviser reader of exactly that wire summary. If the arithmetic were priced you would not see all four published targets sitting above spot (average 6450p, Berenberg buy 5600p reiterated 25 July 2026, and even Jefferies' underperform target of 4015p is 7% above the 3750p spot) and you would not see the whole 19% de-rating since 23 July happen on a median 8,030 shares a day with no analyst revision in between.
evidence.independence: Separately corroborated as a fact pattern by the company's 22 January 2026 statement, which guided FY2026 to 200-250p explicitly 'assuming no rebound in US demand and no contribution from Geotek's next coring expedition' -- and the July RNS then pushed that expedition from early 2027 to 'no earlier than 2028', so the FY26 bar has not moved while the 2027 support under it has been removed: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/judges-scientific-says-starts-2026-with-lower-than-desired-order-book-ce7e58d2de8ff725 (2026-01-22). Note this finding deliberately merges what were two sizes in my pre-local draft (the H2 arithmetic and the order-book framing) because both rest on the same RNS document.

evidence.text: The Investegate regulated-news record shows Judges has filed nothing price-sensitive in the 61 days since it reaffirmed FY2026 -- only a Notice of Investor Presentation (12 Aug) and two Share Incentive Plan PDMR notices (6 Aug, 10 Sep) -- from an issuer that publishes its own consensus number and has a demonstrated habit of putting bad news out in a standalone RNS, which under MAR Article 17 makes two months of silence evidence the board does not presently believe 202.8p is materially unachievable.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three times this board concluded it would miss, it said so in a dedicated RNS and the stock fell double digits the same morning (2024-11-18 -11.61%, 2025-07-24 -15.19%, 2026-01-22 about -11%). The two times it reached September interims without having warned first, the reaction was -4.27% (2024) and +1.91% (2025). So the informative event for this name has historically been the warning RNS, not the results RNS.
evidence.why_not_priced: An absence is not a headline and no aggregator emits it; you can only establish it from a complete domestic RNS mirror, which is what Investegate is. The price is behaving as if a warning were coming -- the stock is at 3750p, 2.7% off its 52-week low of 3650p and 41% below the 6360p high, having fallen 19% from 4625p on 22 July -- but it got there on a median 8,030 shares a day (about GBP 300k), which is a thin tape with no bid rather than a market verdict. If the market had weighed the silence you would expect the drift to have stopped or reversed as the 30-day closed period began around 24 August; instead the stock made new lows on 16, 17, 21 and 22 September. Deliberately sized small and its band crosses zero, because this board has never issued a truly out-of-cycle warning -- it uses its scheduled January and July statements -- and 23 September is itself a scheduled slot it could use.
evidence.independence: The six PDMR notices since July are all automatic Share Incentive Plan or dividend-reinvestment purchases of 6 to 8 shares each at 4450.0p (05/08/2026) and 4175.0p (07/09/2026), so nothing in the insider record contradicts or corroborates the silence in either direction -- there is no discretionary director buying at the low either: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/judges-scientific--jdg/director-pdmr-shareholding/9766456 (2026-09-10).

evidence.text: The bullish half of the baseline's positioning lean is stale and belongs to one manager's profit-taking: the FCA per-holder record shows GLG Partners LP peaked at 1.82% on 2026-02-11 and filed a monotonic 1.78 / 1.68 / 1.58 / 1.47 / 1.36 through 19 May 2026 while the stock fell 41%, and the aggregate has sat at 1.67% since position date 17/08/2026 with no filing in the five weeks since, during which the stock fell another 3.8%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on this name for a short-covering reaction. What the record does show is that the covering flow has not supported the price at any point: GLG [sizing note removed].82% to 1.36% between February and May 2026 and the stock fell from roughly 6000p to 4500p over the same stretch, and it cut again into mid-August while the stock fell from 4550p to 3900p.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sealed baseline read only the aggregated register, which shows one number and one change (1.67%, -0.52pp) and scores it as `short_building` +1.040 -- a bullish component worth nearly half the +2.295 lean. The per-holder history, which only the FCA's own per-holder file and Investegate's mirror of it carry, shows that change is the tail of a seven-month orderly reduction by a single manager into a 41% decline, and that it stopped five weeks before the print. I am NOT claiming the other half of the lean back: 111,234 shares against 8,030 a day is 13.9 sessions to cover and that squeeze constraint is real, but it is already what `short_squeeze` +1.002 is paying for and I will not double-count it. evidence.text: Judges has a written dividend policy of 'increasing dividends by no less than 10% per annum', which implies a 36.0p interim on 23 September against pre-announced H1 adjusted EPS of 38p-42p -- cover of about 1.1x, against 4.3x on the 32.7p paid a year ago.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line has never surprised: the company raised the interim 10% to 32.7p in 2025 and the final 10% to 82.3p at the 31 March 2026 prelims -- a day the stock rose 4.48% on results that the same release called disappointing, with the dividend increase the headline positive most coverage led with.
evidence.why_not_priced: The four analysts will model +10% and the increase itself is not news; what is not modelled anywhere I could reach is that policy compliance now costs the board almost all of first-half earnings, so the declaration is a costly signal rather than a formality and the market is not positioned to read it as one with the stock at a 52-week low. Sized small and with a band that reaches -2.0 because the downside case -- the first break of a policy this company has honoured every year since 2008 -- would be read as a pre-emptive admission about the second half. If the market were pricing that risk the stock would not be holding a roughly 18.5x multiple on the 202.8p consensus.
evidence.independence: The facility terms in the same document make a forced cut unlikely and therefore cap this finding's downside: 'GBP 90m RCF alongside a GBP 50m uncommitted accordion facility ... evidence.text: Solaria's print-day reaction is structurally skewed upward over this window. The release lands in-session with a growth headline, while the call where quality gets questioned comes at 18:00 CET after the close. The stock closed up on D at each of the last five prints (+9.44% on 2025-06-03, +5.27% on 2025-09-30, +15.72% on 2025-11-17, +8.73% on 2026-02-26, +4.31% on 2026-05-18). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: D-day closes computed from Yahoo daily bars, with CNMV filing times. The last five in-session prints were all up: +9.44, +5.27, +15.72, +8.73, +4.31. The two 2024 post-close prints fell on D+1 (-7.58 on the 9M-24 profit cut, +1.83). The largest beat (Q1-26, NP 80 vs 17 est.) was +4.31 on D and then -6.34 on D+1 after the call, so beats are sold on digestion and only D counts here.
evidence.why_not_priced: Had the market priced a print-day pop, the stock would be running up into the release. Instead it is -1.9% over 20 days and -15.6% over 60, fell 3.7% on the seal day, is ~32% below its 26 May close of 24.47, and has disclosed shorts still at 5.6% with fresh quant shorts dated 18 and 21 September. The bar has already moved up after Q1: Sabadell's 92m Q2 EBITDA is +39% year on year. That leaves the edge thinner than in May, which is why the size is small.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior read on squeezes. The Nov-2025 print (+15.72% on D) came while the stock was already rallying. Shorts built through Jul-Aug 2026 as the stock fell 35% (merca2, 12 Aug).

Had it been read as bearish conviction building, the stock would not have held 16-17.5 through September on flat volume.

evidence.text: Man Wah Holdings (HKEX 1999), a sofa maker that counts DFS among its ten largest European customers, has built a DFS stake with its chairman from 3.17% to 10.18% since 30 Jun. It crossed 10% on 22 Sep, the day Yahoo shows 2.34m shares traded against a ~0.25m median. On 31 Aug the listed company bought 7.68m shares from the chairman's family vehicle at £1.623 a share, about 9% above spot, with a stated aim of a 'closer cooperative relationship'. A price-insensitive strategic buyer that is still active into the print cushions a disappointing guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior results day had a live strategic buyer in the register. On 16 Jul 2026 (H2 order intake -4.4%) the stock fell 5.99% while Man Wah's position sat at about 5%. The next day, 17 Jul, it recovered +7.1% (133.5 to 143.0 on Yahoo daily closes, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/DFS.L?range=4mo&interval=1d), and Man Wah crossed 6% on 29 Jul.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only partly priced. The English-language record is a string of TR-1 forms with no commentary. I found no English article framing Man Wah as a strategic or possible bidder, and no mention that it paid 162.3p, above today's price. If the market read this as bid interest the stock would carry a premium to the 162p Man Wah paid. Instead it sits at 148.5, below that and below the 165 of late August. The one visible repricing is today's +7% intraday on 1.36m shares after the 09:05 TR-1, and that is why this is sized small: a good part of it is already in the window's opening price.
evidence.independence: The TR-1 series on Investegate and the HKEX connected-transaction filing are separate documents from separate regulators. They show the same buyer, so this counts as one finding. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0831/2026083100921.pdf

evidence.text: Container freight has roughly doubled into FY27, and DFS itself sizes that exposure: 'every $1,000 movement in freight rate per container impacts our annual freight cost charge by c.£7m-£8m a year'. Drewry Shanghai to Rotterdam ran $4,287-4,682 per FEU from July to August 2026 and $3,626 on 17 Sep, against $2,840 in January 2026, and the composite WCI stood at $1,669-1,959 in Oct-Nov 2025. So a $1,000-1,500 sustained gap is £7-12m against a FY27 consensus of £48.0m that assumes +7% PBT growth on +0.9% revenue.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Freight turned from tailwind into a headwind within FY25: a -120bp gross-margin hit disclosed in the FY25 prelims (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/dfs-furniture--dfs/fy25-preliminary-results/9130219). The stock rose 2.0% that day because the company said it was 'comfortable with consensus'. The last time DFS's outlook disappointed (16 Jul 2026, weaker H2 demand) it fell 5.99%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, so sized small. The sensitivity is in DFS's own FY25 results and the freight index is public, so the sell-side can do this arithmetic. The company-compiled FY27 consensus was refreshed on 16 Sep, after the freight spike, and still shows +7% growth. So either analysts expect mitigation or rates to fall, which is happening: -9% on the week to 17 Sep as Suez reopens. If the market had priced a freight-driven FY27 cut, the FY27 consensus on DFS's own page would sit at or below FY26's £44.8m, not at £48.0m. The residual is a probability-weighted chance the new CFO (Dominique Highfield, on the board since 5 May 2026) guides below that number.
evidence.independence: Drewry WCI via Daily Cargo News, 17 Sep 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-17-september-2026), 2 Jul 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-2-july-2026), 13 Aug 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-13-august-2026) and 8 Jan 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-8-january-2026). This is a different source from the company sensitivity.

Against it, BRC-KPMG August 2026 says 'big-ticket purchases like furniture and household appliances declined' (https://furniturenews.net/news/consumer-demand-cools-as-summer-ends-say-brc-kpmg), and Dunelm on 8 Sep said 'significantly softer trading in first six weeks of FY27', better after the weather cooled (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/dunelm-group--dnlm/preliminary-results-/9759867). Under China's dual-use export ban (MOFCOM, 2026-07-24), the company estimates that about half of semiconductor-materials segment revenue relied on Chinese InP substrates. The segment was 8.8% of 2025 revenue, so about 4% of group revenue is at risk from Q3 onward. The detector and matrix lines are unaffected, with more than a year of substrate stock on hand. The H1 report may quantify this, but the revenue effect falls in H2.

Under the PCO framework annex, the matrix test batch is due in Q4 2026, with a minimum-volume framework of 191.86m PLN for 2027-2032. The 63m PLN ABB at 480 funds that production line, so the financing buys a documented ramp rather than signalling distress.

evidence.text: The interim's outlook is likely to firm or raise FY26 expectations. The company-quoted FY26 revenue consensus of £174.1m, against H1 revenue of £91.1m, implies H2 revenue of about £83.0m, down about 2% on H2 2025's £84.8m (FY25 £163.1m less H1 25 £78.3m). Yet July revenue was +23.9%, the year to date +18.3%, August 'commencing strongly', and the largest UK competitor, Headlam, filed for administration on 1 Sep, entered it on 8 Sep and closed 28 of 76 trade counters with 154 jobs cut on 9 Sep. This will be Likewise's first statement since any of the Headlam events.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Likewise statements with strong revenue momentum were mostly paid: trading updates +7.46% (Dec-23), +12.5% (Jan-24), +11.29% (Dec-24), +4.21% (Jan-25), +8.0% (Jan-26), +4.58% (Jun-26). Reaffirm-only interims were flat to down: -3.75% (Sep-23), -0.36% (Sep-25), with +6.45% in Sep-24. The one profit shortfall (Nov-25) was -12.5%. Source: baseline history, observed RNS dates.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Headlam narrative is partly priced: LIKE rose 31.67p to 35.10p on 1 Sep on about 6.4m shares, 11x average volume, and has held about 34-35p since. What is not priced is the number. No revenue upgrade has been published: the forecast stayed at £174.1m through the AGM (17 Jun) and the fundraise (28 Jul), and there has been no Likewise RNS on trading since 5 Aug. If the market held an upgraded consensus, the stock would not sit only about 4% above its 28 Jul pre-placing close of 33.5p after a +23.9% July and the removal of its largest competitor. Coverage is one house broker (analyst_count null in the baseline), so no one publishes an independent H2 number.
evidence.independence: Headlam side, from different documents: administrators appointed 8 Sep (Headlam RNS via insightDIY, https://www.insightdiy.co.uk/news/headlam-appoints-administrators-updates-on-trading/16829.htm); 28 trade counters closed and 154 jobs cut (GB News, 2026-09-09, https://www.gbnews.com/money/economy-flooring-headlam-cut-jobs). Momentum since the half: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/likewise-group--like/result-of-retail-offer-and-july-update/9706662 (5 Aug: July +23.9%, YTD +18.3%, 'August starting strongly'). All of these point to the same event (the outlook paragraph), so they are merged into one finding, not two.

evidence.text: H1 profit conversion is the risk to the print. Likewise already missed a PBT forecast (Nov 2025) on 'increased costs' despite revenue growth. It only reaffirmed 'in line' at the July fundraise despite revenue running 10pp ahead of the model, cited about £0.5m of annualised extra fuel cost, and is carrying set-up costs for the Leeds 2nd hub, the Newport extension (live July), Corby, 77 new trucks and sales hiring.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last profit-line surprise was Nov-25: 'Underlying Profit Before Tax will fall short of current market forecasts' on +8.9% YTD revenue, and the stock moved -12.5%. At the Sep-25 interim, PBT +120% to £0.74m with a reaffirm moved -0.36%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Weakly unpriced. The market has rewarded revenue headlines (see the history above), and H1 PBT has never been pre-released. If investors were pricing a profit gap, the stock would not trade on about 30x forecast PBT after a +18% 60-day run. The size is small because gross profit alone rose by about £4.6m in H1 (£91.1m x 32.1% against £78.3m x 31.4%), which leaves room to absorb costs; this is a risk, not a document-backed shortfall.
evidence.independence: The fuel-cost caveat and the 'in line' reaffirm despite revenue running ahead are in the 28 Jul fundraise RNS (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/likewise-group--like/proposed-fundraising-to-raise-up-to-29-2-million-/9692164), a different document from the Nov-25 warning.

evidence.text: Tullow's own H1 production (c.43.7 kboepd) is already above the top of its 34-42 kboepd FY range. The operator's partner Kosmos reported Jubilee exiting Q2 above 85k bopd gross, with J50 expected to lift it above 90k bopd. That puts Tullow's Q3 net run-rate near 50 kboepd (c.39% of 90k Jubilee + c.8 TEN + c.7.5 gas). The Aug guide of 'high end of 34-42' looks mechanically too low, so a production raise above the range at the interims is likely.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance-bearing Tullow updates move a lot and in both directions. The FCF upgrade in the 2026-08-05 Trading Statement went to -6.66% (the market focused on flat net debt, per Jefferies via Investing.com). The June 2026 AGM update with 'higher end' language went +8.84%. The H1 2025 results with a guide cut went -18.99%. The last results day after a pre-release trading statement (FY, 2026-04-28) went +11.40%, but the refinancing completion landed the same day. H1 2024 results went +0.87%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Tullow has repeated 'high end of 34-42' three times (FY results, AGM update, Aug TS) while printing above 42 each time, so any model anchored on company language sits at 42 or below. If the market had priced a range raise, the reaction to the 5 Aug statement would not have been -6.7%. Most of the 60-day rally lines up with Brent (80 to about 107 at peak) and with Kosmos moving in step, not with a Tullow-specific volume rerating. Caveat: Kosmos is a public, well-read source and analysts can do this arithmetic, so most of it is probably known. That is why the size is small.
evidence.independence: Tullow's own 5 Aug RNS: H1 43.7 kboepd, J76 'significantly above expectations', J77 and J50 onstream (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/tullow-oil--tlw/trading-statement/9704842). evidence.text: The FY26 FCF guide ($170-250m at $70-100/bbl) rests on Jan-Jul realisations of c.$93/bbl. Brent front-month traded roughly $88-109 from mid-August to 24 Sep. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last FCF upgrade (2026-08-05, from $70-175m to $170-250m) was sold: -6.66% on the day. The June AGM update with FCF upside framing went +8.84%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The stock is up about 43% since 14 Aug alongside Brent, and oil is a public series. What stays unpriced is only the step from 'implied' to 'company-stated'. This finding and the first one both land on the same guidance line, so together they count as one guide raise and are sized that way.

positioning.basis: The KNF register is a DataTables POST to `rss.knf.gov.pl/RssOuterView/JSCRIPT`, which answers 302 without a cookie and 403 with one, on every attempt and with browser headers. This is a HARD failure, not the intermittent kind: on the same sweep `www.gpw.pl` and `espi.pap.pl` each scored 0 of 8 while `emarketstorage.com` scored 7 of 8. So a Polish name has NO positioning anchor.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. FOR THIS NAME THE LEAN IS THE RUN-UP ALONE, because the national short register could not be read -- so the baseline's lean and the free control are the same number and the control cannot be beaten by anything using it.
